audit.corrected: No chart edits. Phase text sharpened with Nevermove's 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s and Death's Hand's 7/6/5/4/3s so the even rows have countable windows.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[1] names 'Grand Hegemony', which is not a Swain ability. Nevermove is also described as a plain delayed root, with no mention of the return trip or the follow-up pull.
audit.why: Swain's passive is Ravenous Flock — ravens collect Soul Fragments that heal him and permanently raise his max health, which is where his ramp actually comes from. Nevermove launches a wave forward that roots only when it RETURNS to him, after which he can pull every rooted champion closer; that return timing is the entire dodge, and the pull is what feeds you into Death's Hand, whose bolts stack extra damage per bolt.
audit.corrected: Fabricated name replaced with Ravenous Flock's Soul Fragments; the return-trip root and the pull stated in early, spikes[0], mid, wants.you[0] and wants.foe[0].

audit.why: Nevermove at 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s is the punishable window and the page already commits to it.

edits.before: Skill phase: Swain wants to land W (Vision of Empire) and E (Nevermove) to root you for his Q barrage, but if you dodge the slow-moving E with E (Ashen Pursuit) you can punish his long cooldowns with Q marks and on-hits.
edits.after: Skill phase: Swain wants W (Vision of Empire) and E (Nevermove) to root you for his Q barrage, but Nevermove only roots on its return trip — sidestep that with E (Ashen Pursuit) and punish the 12-second cooldown with Q marks and on-hits.

edits.before: Skill lane early — Swain's main threat is E (Nevermove), a delayed root that sets up his Q (Death's Hand) barrage, so bait or dodge it with your E (Ashen Pursuit) blink. When his root and W are down he's exposed; step in for Q (Ritual Nails) marks and Silver Stake on-hits.
edits.after: Skill lane early — Swain's E (Nevermove) roots on the way BACK, not the way out, and lets him pull you into a Q (Death's Hand) barrage, so sidestep the return with your E (Ashen Pursuit) blink. When his root and W are down he's exposed; step in for Q (Ritual Nails) marks and free on-hits.

edits.before: Through 4-5 it stays even and revolves around his E cooldown — eat a root and you take a big Q combo, dodge it and you win the trade. Use W (Soul Ignition) grey-health to survive his poke while you close the gap on his long-cooldown windows.
edits.after: Through 4-5 it stays even and revolves around his E's 12-to-10-second cooldown — eat the return root and he pulls you into a full Q combo; dodge it and the trade is yours. Use W (Soul Ignition) grey-health to ride out his Q poke while you close.

edits.before: Dodge his E (Nevermove) root with E (Ashen Pursuit) so his Q combo whiffs
edits.after: Dodge the Nevermove return with E (Ashen Pursuit) so his pull whiffs

edits.before: Land E (Nevermove) into a full Q (Death's Hand) barrage while W-marked
edits.after: Root you on the Nevermove return, pull you in, then barrage with Q

edits.before: Ramp Grand Hegemony stacks so his R sustain outlasts your burst
edits.after: Collect Ravenous Flock fragments so his R sustain outlasts you

notes: 'Grand Hegemony' is not a Swain ability — his passive is Ravenous Flock, and the Soul Fragments it collects are the real source of the heal-plus-permanent-max-health ramp the page was gesturing at. The bigger practical fix is Nevermove: it roots on the RETURN trip and then lets him pull rooted champions in, so 'dodge the slow-moving E' was aiming players at the wrong half of the cast.
